newsitem.title: USA: U.S. health groups attack tobacco deal provision.
newsitem.headline: U.S. health groups attack tobacco deal provision.

text.p: Leading U.S. public health advocates overwhelmingly rejected a key part of the proposed tobacco deal, calling any restrictions on the Food and Drug Administration's ability to regulate nicotine "unacceptable."

The recommendations of the nation's leading public health organiations are not binding but are expected to carry great weight as Congress considers complex legislation that would be necessary to enact the proposed $368 billion tobacco deal.
The panel of public health care groups was formed at the behest of some anti-tobacco lawmakers and is headed by former FDA commissioner David Kessler and former Surgeon General C. Everett Koop.

It is reviewing the main points of the 68-page deal and has not yet ruled on the overall package. But the panel was vehement on demanding that the FDA "continue to have immediate and explicit authority to regulate" nicotine, members said.

The agreement between the cigarette companies and some state attorney generals set conditions on FDA authority which, the health advocates argue, would effectively allow the tobacco industry to fend off regulation.
"It is absolutely unacceptable," Dudley Hafner, head of the American Heart Association, told reporters.
